events.category: Japan / Afro-Cuban Latin jazz / Trumpet-led ensemble
events.factual_description: Luis Valle & Afro Qbamigos! present “Akasaka Summertime” at Jazz Dining B-flat in Akasaka, Tokyo, on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. Doors are at 6:00 PM and the performance starts at 7:00 PM. Valle's official event page announces a seven-person lineup: Luis Valle on trumpet, flugelhorn and vocal; Andy Wulf on saxophone and chorus; Chie Suzuki on vibraphone and marimba; Masaru Okuyama on piano; Tetsuo Koizumi on bass; Kenji Imafuku on percussion; and Setsu Fujii on drums. The page describes the band's language as rooted in Cuban music and combining jazz, Afro-Cuban music and salsa, and calls this Akasaka Summertime edition a one-night special ensemble. The published music charge is ¥5,000 plus tax for general admission and ¥4,000 plus tax for students, with one drink and one food order additionally required. The venue address published by the artist is Akasaka Sakae Building B1F, 6-6-4 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052.

en.why_it_matters: This is a useful window into Tokyo's international jazz ecology: a Havana-born trumpeter who has worked from Japan since 1997 leading a septet where trumpet and flugelhorn sit beside saxophone and vibraphone/marimba over piano, bass, percussion and drums. Afro Qbamigos turns the Cuba–Japan connection into sound, folding Afro-Cuban and salsa rhythm into a jazz setting with real room for improvisation. The one-night Akasaka Summertime frame gives the club date a specific shape without pretending the active band itself is disappearing.
en.trip_verdict: If September 29 is open in Tokyo, this is a strong choice for a Latin-leaning club night, especially if the trip is tracing the city's international jazz ecology. Attend if the evening lines up naturally; I would keep a scarcer master, farewell, premiere or true one-off ahead of it.

es.why_it_matters: Es una buena ventana a la ecología internacional del jazz de Tokio: un trompetista nacido en La Habana y radicado musicalmente en Japón desde 1997 al frente de un septeto donde trompeta y fliscorno conviven con saxofón y vibráfono/marimba sobre piano, bajo, percusión y batería. Afro Qbamigos convierte la conexión Cuba–Japón en sonido, metiendo ritmo afrocubano y salsa dentro de un entorno de jazz con espacio real para la improvisación. El marco de una sola noche de Akasaka Summertime le da forma concreta a la fecha de club sin fingir que la banda activa está por desaparecer.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 29 de septiembre está libre en Tokio, es una muy buena opción para una noche de club con inclinación latina, sobre todo si el viaje viene siguiendo la ecología internacional del jazz de la ciudad. Vale ir si la noche acomoda naturalmente; mantendría por delante a un maestro más escaso, una despedida, un estreno o una fecha verdaderamente irrepetible.
